title: Free energy spectroscopy reveals the mechanistic landscape of chromatin compaction.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 17210278 metadata (one 62 MB zip, CC-BY, titled 'tetra-nucl-FE-simulations: Simulations Scripts and Data'); its GitHub mirror file tree (169 files, 211 MB uncompressed, 66 files named COLVARS); and one COLVARS file downloaded in full (20,004 lines, header '#! FIELDS time d12 d13 d14 d23 d24 d34 e2e d13_minus_d24', no units given). Searched for the stated Mendeley Data deposit of the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images: no identifier in the paper text, none in the PubMed Central HTML, and zero hits on DataCite for the title, for a Mendeley deposit by the first author, or for 'chromatin nanocaliper'. Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice, so Supplementary Tables S3-S5 (particle counts per condition and per distance bin) were not retrievable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That TEM images exist in Mendeley Data; that end-to-end distances were measured manually in ImageJ and exported as per-point CSV files; that particle counts are listed in Supplementary Tables S3 and S5; that 66 GPU molecular dynamics (MD) simulations totalling 2 microseconds were run with OpenMM and a coarse-grained model. None of the per-particle measurements, image counts or supplementary tables were seen.

a1_downloadable.note: The experimental data has no working link. The data statement says TEM images are 'deposited at Mendeley data' but gives no DOI or accession anywhere in the text or PubMed Central HTML, DataCite returns nothing for it, and everything else is 'available from the lead contact upon request'. Only the 62 MB Zenodo zip of MD simulation scripts and collective-variable output downloads.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For the simulation data that does download, free energy is not a column: the COLVARS files hold biased distance trajectories and the free energy landscape must be reconstructed by weighted-histogram reweighting across the 66 biased windows. For the TEM route, the per-particle end-to-end distances (the label) are not deposited at all, only, reportedly, the raw images.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs for the simulation route are present: coarse-grained structure files plus 66 collective-variable time series I opened. TEM images themselves were never located.

a4_units_stated.note: The COLVARS header I opened lists distances d12...d34, e2e with no units; the paper discusses nanometres and kcal/mol but the files carry no unit row or README mapping columns to units.

a5_enough_rows.note: The independent unit in the downloadable data is the simulation window: 66 of them (each ~20,000 correlated time frames, which are not independent examples). Experimental particle counts are in Supplementary Table S5, which I could not retrieve.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 211 MB uncompressed; the 66 COLVARS tables together are ~120 MB of plain text and stream easily in 16 GB RAM.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper says 66 MD simulations; the repository contains exactly 66 COLVARS output files, which matches.

a8_label_provenance.note: The free energy label in the downloadable data is produced by the coarse-grained force field itself, i.e. computed from the same coordinates that would be the features. Training on it distils the simulation model rather than learning from a physical measurement. The one physically measured quantity (manual TEM end-to-end distance) is not in any accessible file.

existing_models.name: Deep neural network pipeline for dynamic DNA origami devices (YOLOv5 object detector plus ResNet50 classifier), Scientific Reports 2023, from the same DNA origami nanocaliper group
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as automating particle detection and conformation/pose estimation on raw TEM micrographs of DNA origami nanocalipers; I read the search summary and abstract only, so no number or split is verified here.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not verified - I did not retrieve the discussion section.

existing_models.name: Convolutional neural networks for characterising DNA origami in TEM images (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2025), pretrained on 720 simulated images and fine-tuned on 146 experimental TEM images
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked nine standard backbones (AlexNet through ResNet152) for ligation-number classification; VGG16 best after fine-tuning. Numbers not verified from the paper itself.

backbone.name: None appropriate: ResNet-style image backbones would fit TEM particle crops, but the particle crops and their manual distance labels are not downloadable.
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for small image crops if they existed
backbone.licence: Zenodo simulation code/data is CC-BY-4.0; TEM image licence unknown because the deposit was not found.

integration.partner_dataset: None identified: the data carries no standard biological identifier (no UniProt, Ensembl, PDB or chemical key), only simulation window labels and pixel coordinates.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - there is no identifier in this data that joins it to any large public resource.

controls.positive_control: Would have been recovering the known nucleosome-stacking distance minimum (~6 nm inter-nucleosome distance) and the known magnesium dependence of compaction.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle window labels across the 66 umbrella windows and confirm the reconstructed landscape collapses.
controls.external_validation: None accessible: the independent TEM measurement that would validate the simulation landscape is the part of the data that is not deposited with a findable identifier.

honest_claim_h3: With only coarse-grained simulation output available, any model could claim at most 'reproduces the free energy surface of one specific coarse-grained tetranucleosome force field, from 66 biased windows', which is a statement about the simulation, not about chromatin.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use electron microscope images of DNA nanodevices to predict how tightly a four-nucleosome chromatin unit is folded.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered was: individual TEM (transmission electron microscope) particle images of a DNA origami 'nanocaliper' holding one tetranucleosome, across magnesium and linker-histone conditions. Number of particles unknown - the counts live in a supplementary table I could not retrieve.
plain_idea.predict: The nanocaliper's end-to-end distance and the nucleosome stacking state, whose true values come from a human placing points by hand on each particle in ImageJ.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Biophysics labs measuring chromatin compaction one particle at a time would get free energy landscapes without weeks of manual clicking; even a failure would quantify how reproducible manual TEM measurement is.

more_or_better_data.why: The published DNA origami TEM deep-learning work was fine-tuned on 146 experimental images and 720 simulated ones; I cannot claim more data because this paper's image set has no findable deposit and its particle counts are in an unretrievable supplementary table.

confidence_score.why: Per-particle measurements are not deposited, so replicate human measurements of the same particle - the only route to a noise estimate here - are unavailable.

models_beatable.why: The closest existing work (YOLOv5 plus ResNet50 on nanocaliper TEM, 2023; nine-backbone CNN benchmark, 2025) is recent, uses standard pretrained vision backbones, and comes from the same community, so there is no obvious weakness to exploit.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: we cannot run the existing model's data or our own, because the images and their labels are not obtainable.

ml_idea: Intended idea: a vision model that takes a cropped TEM image of a DNA origami nanocaliper plus tetranucleosome and outputs end-to-end distance (regression) and stacking state (classification), replacing manual ImageJ measurement and extending free energy spectroscopy to many conditions. Blocked because the images have no locatable deposit and the manual measurements are not released. Fallback idea on the available simulation data - learn the tetranucleosome free energy surface from the 66 umbrella windows - fails because the label is the force field's own output.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the file sizes I listed: 169 files, 211 MB uncompressed, largest single table 1.9 MB of text; nothing was timed because no model was planned.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a Mendeley Data DOI for the TEM images - it is absent from the paper, PubMed Central and DataCite, which kills the project in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Part A1, A2, A4, A5 and A8 fail. The experimental data that matters - TEM images and the per-particle end-to-end distances measured by hand - is announced as 'deposited at Mendeley data' with no DOI, accession or link anywhere in the paper or PubMed Central, is not in DataCite, and the rest is explicitly 'available from the lead contact upon request'. The only thing that does download (verified) is a 62 MB Zenodo zip of coarse-grained molecular dynamics scripts plus 66 umbrella-sampling collective-variable files with unlabelled units; there the label (free energy) must be reconstructed by reweighting and originates from the simulation force field itself, so a model would distil the simulation rather than learn biology, with only 66 independent units. Separately, automated analysis of DNA origami nanocaliper TEM images has already been published twice (2023 YOLOv5 plus ResNet50; 2025 CNN benchmark), so even with the images this would be a crowded task.
